title: Bellhop server-to-agent message, protocol version 1
description: Every message a server may send. Implementations MUST ignore message types and object fields they do not recognise, so validation should be advisory rather than enforced on the receiving side.

printOptions.title: print options
printOptions.description: How to print the job (PROTOCOL.md §5.2.3). Every option is optional; an absent option means whatever the target printer does by default. Note additionalProperties: false, which is deliberate and unique in this protocol. Everywhere else an unrecognised field MUST be ignored; here that would mean printing something other than what was asked for and acking success, so the set is closed and an agent MUST fail a job carrying anything else. Two rules this schema cannot express and the agent MUST enforce: which options apply to which format, and whether the target printer can honor a value.

copies.description: Applies to every format. For zpl and raw the agent delivers the byte stream this many times rather than asking CUPS or the printer to duplicate it. The ceiling is a blast radius rather than a technical limit: copies is the one option whose bug is spent physical stock.

duplex.description: pdf only. long-edge and short-edge require capabilities.duplex true on the target; otherwise the job fails with unsupported_value.

paper.description: pdf and gif. MUST be one of the strings the agent reported in that printer's capabilities.papers. Matching is exact string equality: the agent never normalises or translates a media keyword, because a guess here comes out of the machine as a label on the wrong stock.

bin.description: pdf and gif. MUST be one of the strings the agent reported in that printer's capabilities.bins.

dpi.description: pdf and gif. MUST be one of the integers the agent reported in that printer's capabilities.dpi.

color.description: pdf and gif. true requires capabilities.color true on the target. Either value requires that the target reported the field at all: an absent capability is unknown, not permission.

pages.description: pdf only. One-based, no spaces. The pattern cannot express the remaining rules, which the agent MUST enforce with invalid_option: terms ascending, non-overlapping, and first no greater than last.

rotate.description: pdf and gif. Degrees clockwise, always, because a rotation whose direction is a matter of opinion is a label printed upside down half the time.

fit.description: pdf and gif. Scale the document to the media. Defaults to true, which is what agents already did before this option existed; false prints at natural size and clips.

collate.description: pdf only. With more than one copy, 1,2,3,1,2,3 rather than 1,1,2,2,3,3. Harmless and unobservable with one copy or one page, which is not an error.

ready.title: ready
ready.description: Response to hello, and the only message a server may send before it. Folds branding and the credential into the handshake so they are not separate messages on every reconnect.

protocol_version.description: MUST equal the agent's version if the server accepted the session; otherwise close with 4002 instead of sending ready.

credential.description: The current licence credential. Servers SHOULD always include it: this is what makes renewal invisible.

heartbeat_seconds.description: Requested agent keepalive interval. The agent clamps out-of-range values.

print.title: print
print.description: Print one document. Exactly one of url and data must be present; if both are, the agent uses data. A job that names no printer routes by format to a role in the agent's default_printers.

id.description: Opaque, unique per pairing, never reused. Echoed in ack and used by the agent to suppress duplicates. A rejected job counts as completed in that ledger, so a job corrected after a failed ack needs a new id.

kind.description: App-defined and opaque to the agent. Shown in the agent's recent activity list.

format.description: zpl and raw are delivered to the queue untouched; pdf and gif are rendered. Decides routing when the job names no printer: zpl, raw and gif to the label role, pdf to the document role. MUST be covered by a print:<format> capability from the agent's hello.

printer.description: The id of a printer from the agent's most recent hello. Overrides format routing. A job naming a printer the agent has not shared MUST fail with error_code unknown_printer, and that failure deliberately does not distinguish an unshared printer from one that does not exist.

url.description: HTTPS URL (http permitted only for localhost). At most 3 redirects, 30s timeout, 50 MB ceiling. The agent sends no credentials, so the URL must carry its own authorisation.

data.description: Base64 of the document bytes, up to 50 MB decoded. Preferred for ZPL.

config.title: config
config.description: Mid-session branding update. Everything in it also appears in ready, so a server that only sets branding at connect time never needs to send this.

credential.title: credential
credential.description: Mid-session licence update. The agent verifies it offline and adopts it only if it verifies; an invalid one is logged and discarded, leaving the previous credential in place.

ping.title: ping
ping.description: Keepalive. The agent MUST reply with pong echoing token.

pong.title: pong
pong.description: Response to an agent ping. Answering this is the one mandatory, easily forgotten server obligation.

close.title: close
close.description: Advisory sent immediately before the server closes the transport, for frameworks that cannot set a WebSocket close code, for the HTTP transport, which has no close frame, and for carrying retry_after_seconds, which no close frame has room for.

code.description: Any code of PROTOCOL.md §7.1: 4001 unauthorized, 4002 unsupported_version, 4003 agent_deactivated (all terminal); 4004 superseded and 4005 try_other_transport are retryable; 1000, 1001, 1012 and anything else retry on backoff.

retry_after_seconds.description: Pacing hint for the reconnect that follows (PROTOCOL.md §7.3). Applies to the next attempt only; the agent randomises within [half, whole]. Meaningful only with retryable codes; ignored on terminal codes.
